title: Sticky-routing chaos escape and graceful fallback for mixed Hosted/Dedicated cross-region incidents
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Summary: During a recent multi-region latency spike, a small percentage of tenants experienced persistent routing to a degraded Dedicated cluster because of our 'sticky routing' decision and an edge prefilter that incorrectly classified a regional health signal. That sticky routing prevented automated cross-region fallback and caused repeated customer escalations for latency-sensitive workloads. Goals: 1) Implement a chaos-escape path that breaks sticky affinity when downstream health signals indicate degraded tail latency or repeated 5xxs for N minutes; 2) Add a short-circuit KV-cache reconciliation and signed short-lived affinity tokens so new requests won't reuse stale routing decisions; 3) Create a tested, low-risk runbook for on-call to trigger graceful fan-out and rollback that works for both Hosted and Dedicated tenants. Design constraints/considerations: - Must preserve tenant isolation guarantees for Dedicated customers (no cross-tenant spillover) while enabling cross-region fallback for customer traffic when appropriate. - Avoid increased tail latency for normal requests: escape path should be evaluated only when error/latency thresholds are breached. - Be conservative about token TTLs to keep affinity benefits for normal workloads. High-level approach: - Routing shim: add a weighted decision layer that checks (a) per-tenant recent 5xx rate and p50/p95 latency samples, (b) signed affinity token TTL, (c) whether KV-cache state is desynced. If any of the failure predicates trip, issue a short-circuit token to allow temporary stateless routing and KV-cache re-prime. - KV reconciliation: on short-circuit, trigger a background KV cache rehydrate for that tenant, with a backoff and a single-rollforward attempt to avoid stampeding. - Safety and rollback: escape path starts in 'monitoring-only' (no action) for 24 hours in staging, then 'canary' with 1% of critical tenants, then 10%, then global. If a fallback increases 5xxs by >2x or customer latency by >30% for >10 minutes, automatically revert to previous affinity behavior and surface an incident. Runbook (TL;DR): 1) Detect: automated alert from cross-region routing SLO and per-tenant 5xx spike. 2) Triage: confirm region-level health dashboards and tenant-specific traces. 3) Short-term mitigation: toggle routing shim from 'normal' to 'escape-canary' for affected tenant group; monitor for KV cache re-prime success. 4) If mitigation helps, ramp by 3x every 10 minutes to 10% then 100% with continued monitoring. 5) If mitigation worsens, rollback to 'normal' and open a debug session (see incident artifacts). Observability: new tracing span added "routing.escape_check" with metadata (tenant_id, token_ttl, desync_reason) and a dashboard tile for short-circuit counts, success rate of cache rehydrates, and correlated latency/5xx deltas. Testing plan: unit tests for token generation/validation, integration test that simulates stale affinity + cached KV mismatch, full staging chaos run that injects region 3s tail latencies and verifies escape triggers. Docs & comms: update Dedicated onboarding docs to explain escape behavior, add customer-facing FAQ for enterprise customers about failover semantics. Artifacts: design doc in Confluence (link in links), a prototype PR for the routing shim, and an internal demo run recording for SRE training.
